The shape with three sides is a triangle.

Regarding the economic theories presented, both Keynesian and supply-side economics share the common goal of achieving economic growth. However, they differ significantly in their methodologies. Keynesian economists advocate for increased government spending to stimulate the economy, especially during downturns, positioning the government as the primary engine. In contrast, supply-side economists argue for lower taxes and reduced government spending to encourage private sector growth, placing the private sector as the primary driver.
